newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik government, opposition agree on refugees.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government, opposition agree on refugees.

text.p: Tajikistan government officials and opposition leaders on Monday signed an accord in Tehran on repatriating thousands of refugees to the turbulent Central Asian country, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

Under the agreement, the government agreed to help the refugees and people displaced by four years of bloody conflict to return home, help in the restitution of their property and guarantee their rights, the agency said.
The accord also included an amnesty under which the government pledged not to prosecute the returnees for taking part in the civil war, it added.

Tajik Foreign Minister Talbak Nazarov, the head of the Islamic opposition delegation Akbar Turajonzada and United Nations special envoy Gerd Merrem, and Iranian and Russian diplomats attended the talks which led to the accord.

The week-long talks covered details of an accord signed in Moscow last month by Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri, which called for an immediate ceasefire, an amnesty, an exchange of war prisoners and the creation of a Commission of National Reconciliation.
The Tehran talks appeared to have failed to resolve disagreements over the composition of the commission which was one of the main issues under discussion.
Before the agreement was signed, Merrem said the quota set aside for each side in the commission and in a future cabinet was "still hanging in the balance", IRNA reported.

Iranian media said the opposition had proposed that the government and the Islamic rebels each get a 40 percent representation on the commission, with the remaining 20 percent going to another opposition group.
The government wanted 80 percent of seats on the 40-member commission for itself and its allies, the media reports said.

Tens of thousand of people have been killed in the civil war spawned by the collapse of the Soviet Union in the country of nearly 6 million people pitting the secular Moscow-backed government against Islamist guerrillas.
Some 60,000 Tajik refugees fled to neighbouring Afghanistan during the civil war which the opposition lost in 1992.
A 96-member U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) works with a much larger peacekeeping force fielded by Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States.
The rebels control the mountainous eastern half of Tajikistan, where about 10 percent of the population live.
